answer: With a Code contribution approved in peer review backed by a time-locked stake, the network asks for proof of craft before proof of personhood: the code contribution is reviewed line by line, the time-locked stake is released only when the work is accepted, and a rejected submission costs the applicant time and money, so fakes must pass the same review bar as honest contributors. One knoll proves nothing on its own; the proof is in the whole pattern of accepted work. When the vault settles over the saffron, the work holds because every task carried its own review.
